access_note: Free for academic and non-profit use; commercial users need an OMNEST licence.
description: OMNeT++ is an extensible, modular, component-based C++ simulation library and framework, used mainly to build network simulators. Models are assembled from reusable modules described in the NED language and configured through ini files; the model frameworks built on it include INET (Internet protocols, wired and wireless links, mobility; release 4.7.0 of July 2026 added satellite and GNSS track mobility and IPv6 parity), Simu5G for cellular 5G, Veins for vehicular networks and many others. OMNeT++ itself is maintained by OpenSim Ltd., which sells a commercial version called OMNEST; the current series is 6.x, with 6.4.0 released in 2026 alongside a preview of AI assistance in the Qtenv interface. Coverage: generic simulation technology with no geographic limitation; network scale ranges from a few nodes to thousands. Format and access: C++ source and installers for Linux, macOS and Windows downloaded from the website, with an Eclipse-based IDE and the Qtenv graphical runtime. Licence and cost: free of charge under the Academic Public License for non-commercial teaching and research; commercial use requires an OMNEST licence. Caveats: the licence restricts commercial use; performance for very large networks depends on parallel simulation settings; protocol fidelity depends on the chosen model framework. Simulation uses: packet-level network flow, capacity planning and resilience studies of communication networks, cascading-failure and co-simulation work that couples communications with power grids or transport. Related records: ns-3 is the main open alternative, Simu5G runs on OMNeT++, and SNDlib or CAIDA topologies can feed network models.
